name: Fantastical Local Calendars
description: Fantastical Local Calendars is the device-local Fantastical surface for viewing and changing On My Mac calendars, reminders, contacts-derived birthdays, events, tasks, calendar sets, and schedules through the installed Mac app.
agentUseSummary: Fantastical Local Calendars cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because On My Mac data requires macOS Calendar, Reminders, and Contacts permissions and Fantastical's installed local sync, while its official MCP, Shortcuts, AppleScript, and URL integrations remain device-local authorities that Relay Marketplace does not currently ship.

blocked.label: Connect local calendars
blocked.description: Relay does not present a Flexibits Account, account key, Apple account, local Calendar store, macOS permission, or installed-app state as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Use Fantastical automation
blocked.description: Fantastical's official Mac MCP connector, App Shortcuts, AppleScript, URL handler, share extension, and system service require the installed app and local permissions that Relay cannot currently mount.

blocked.label: Access local calendar data
blocked.description: Relay does not request Apple, calendar, or Flexibits credentials; inspect EventKit or local app state; reuse account sessions; automate app UI; or infer local calendar authority from Flexibits collaboration services.

blocked.label: Change local calendar items
blocked.description: Searching, reading, creating, editing, moving, inviting, responding to, rescheduling, or deleting local events, tasks, reminders, calendars, and calendar sets remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit local execution and approval boundaries.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Mac-local Fantastical connector using supported automation and explicit Calendar, Reminders, and Contacts permissions.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Fantastical's Mac-local MCP connector, Apple automation, or private On My Mac calendar stores.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Fantastical's Mac-local MCP connector, Apple automation, or private On My Mac calendar stores.

providerSetup.blocker: Fantastical requires macOS Calendar and Reminders permissions, Contacts permission for birthdays and invitations, and local Calendar sync to use On My Mac calendars. Its official MCP connector, App Shortcuts, AppleScript, URL handler, extensions, and system service execute through the installed app. Flexibits states that event, task, contact, and calendar-account credentials remain on device, and its separate Zapier API key covers Openings and Proposals triggers with no actions rather than direct local calendar access. Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution and cannot truthfully expose this authority from Railway.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a Flexibits Account key, Zapier API key, Apple or calendar credentials, or macOS permissions; inspect EventKit or app state; install the Fantastical MCP connector; automate the app; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a separately disclosed Mac-local connection architecture with app presence, explicit Calendar, Reminders, and Contacts permissions, pinned reviewed tools, per-action approval, result redaction, audit, and no cloud fallback.

evidence.supports: Flexibits states that On My Mac calendars require Fantastical to receive macOS Calendar and Reminders permissions, Contacts permission for birthdays and invitations, and local Calendar sync enabled inside the installed app.
Flexibits documents a Mac-only Fantastical MCP connector installed into Claude Desktop with local tools for searching, creating, updating, and deleting events and per-tool permission settings.
Fantastical documents Apple Shortcuts on Mac and iOS for finding local calendars and items, reading schedules and invitees, creating events and tasks, and changing app state.
Fantastical documents local AppleScript and URL-handler automation that can parse and immediately create events in the installed Mac app.
Flexibits states that calendar credentials, events, tasks, and contacts are generally stored on device and not sent to Flexibits, with account passwords or OAuth tokens held in the device keychain.
Fantastical's account API key is documented only for Zapier triggers involving Openings, Proposals, and RSVP responses; the integration offers no Fantastical actions or direct local-calendar API.
